chapter: Lydian book publication and marriage to Juanita
title: Marriage with Juanita and working on the Concept
summary: They married within months, lived in a hotel by her office, and she supported him while he worked on the Concept.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Okay. Take us from there. What happened?

She said, uh-hmm. They left, but she made an impression on me. Six months later or so I called her at her home in Jamaica, with her mother, her father – a Philippine father – and the grandmother, who was an extremely suspicious lady and overseer. I said, “I’d like to take you out to dinner.” That did it. I think a month or two after that we got married, against Grandma’s best wishes. I was – as I said, I was living with John at the time. She was working at New York Life. She had a steady job at New York Life. That was okay. We had to – the first thing we did was get an expensive – too expensive for us – we got a house overlooking the river and all that, Hudson River. That lasted for about two weeks. The money wasn’t there. So we moved to a hotel one block from her New York Life building down at 23rd Street, so that when she’d go to work, she’d just roll out of bed and roll into work. But she was late every day.
So we got married. It was kind of a thing where I said – that happened for about a year. She worked. I didn’t have anything. I worked at this.
Yeah, and I told her that at one point she wouldn’t have to work anymore, that this is going to make it.

She went along. It was – she kept her job, and then she moved to an awful job, reading newspapers and having to check on certain companies that wanted their name in the paper. I forget what they call that, but certain people want their names – they want you to see and preserve their names when their names appeared in the paper.
So she changed jobs and was doing that.
I see. How long were you all together?
